info.desc: "El Camino" is the seventh studio album by American rock duo the Black Keys. It was co-produced by Danger Mouse and the group, and was released on Nonesuch Records on December 6, 2011. The record was the band's follow-up to their commercial breakthrough "Brothers", and was their third collaboration with Danger Mouse. "El Camino" draws from popular genres of the 1950s to 1970s, such as rock and roll, glam rock, rockabilly, surf rock and soul. Danger Mouse contributed as a co-writer on each of the 11 songs alongside guitarist Dan Auerbach and drummer Patrick Carney. .

podcast.body: Released just 19 months after *Brothers* in 2011, following multiple tours. Danger Mouse served as the full-time producer, joining the band in Nashville in the spring of 2011. Recording occurred at Dan Auerbach's newly acquired studio, Easy Eye Sound, providing a relaxed environment with functional gear. The band commenced recording without any pre-written material, composing songs around short hooks inspired by favorite bands such as The Beatles, The Clash, The Cramps, Elvis, and The Ramones, with Danger Mouse co-writing all 11 tracks. The album's cover features a simple image of an old Chrysler van, reminiscent of "The Grey Ghost," their former touring vehicle. *El Camino* achieved massive success, with platinum sales worldwide and triple-platinum status in Canada, a key market for the band. It won a Grammy for Best Rock Album, and its single "Lonely Boy" earned two additional awards, while Dan Auerbach also secured Producer of the Year. "Love that video with Derek T. Tuggle's dancing. That's Lonely Boy from the Black Keys seventh studio album called El Camino."

podcast.body: The seventh studio album, released just 19 months after *Brothers*, following a period of intense touring. Recorded in Nashville in spring 2011 at Dan Auerbach's Easy Eye Sound studio, with Danger Mouse producing the entire record and co-writing all 11 tracks. The album's songs were composed around short hooks inspired by favorite bands like The Beatles, The Clash, The Cramps, Elvis, and The Ramones, simplifying the creative process as they had no finished music upon entering the studio. The album cover features an old Chrysler van, similar to their "Grey Ghost" tour vehicle. It achieved huge success, with platinum sales globally and triple platinum in Canada, where it was a best-performing territory. It won Best Rock Album at the Grammys, and two other awards went to its single "Lonely Boy," while Dan Auerbach won Producer of the Year. "Huge success. Platinum sales around the planet. Triple platinum in Canada by the way, where, with about half the population of the UK, we bought almost as many copies."
